ambient: A flock of starlings darkens the sky over the burnt wood.
The river runs cold this season. The trout are larger.
Bear sign on the south path — claw marks four feet up the pine.
Wolves heard last night across three valleys. Coordinated. Hunting.
An eagle drops a hare at the foot of the high pass. Hungry, evidently.
A dead deer in the meadow, intact, no marks. The crows won't touch it.
Salt deposits in the lower stones. Every prey species came through this week.
Frost in the high pass already. Two weeks early.
A doe stares at the cave system for an hour, then runs.
The reed marsh smells of rot. Something big died and sank.
Twin lion cubs spotted on the tall grass ridge. Heavy with milk.
Three wolverines crossed the open meadow at dawn, fearless.
A pup tries its first howl. Comes out as a yelp.
An old wolf is left behind by the pack. He does not follow.
Mating calls from the boulder field every night for a week.
Strange tracks near old oaks. Five toes. Not a paw print.
A bear ignores a salmon to chase a butterfly. Drunk on spring.
The marsh ducks have arrived. Their meat is fat after the long flight.
An eagle and a falcon fight over a hare. The hare escapes.
